objective: Port portable Transport behavior and original tests using CLR-native Tasks, delegates, sockets and explicit executor dispatch; preserve original comments and test intent. Preserve corresponding Java variable and method identifiers, allowing only the requested C# capitalization/underscore adaptations.
statusMeaning: pending means unreviewed, not automatically a missing CLR feature. in-progress records implemented counterparts with explicit remaining comment/contract/test review. verified test entries cover every declared original test in that fixture with documented CLR adaptations; supplemental tests are not original fixture completion. clr-adapted accounts only for the named source contract. No placeholder counts as ported. A clr-adapted fixture may contain per-method clr-not-applicable decisions only with source contract/reason/real CLR evidence. These methods are reviewed but never counted as mapped original cases or skipped CLR tests. BCL-replaced JVM wrapper roles are clr-adapted with clrReplacement evidence. Wrapper-only comments retain exact text and explicit dispositions; this comment rule is forbidden for test entries. Such roles are not new physical C# wrapper files. deprecated-not-ported and jvm-only-replaced (2026-11-16 owner decisions, notPortedPolicy) record Java units that are deliberately not ported as code; they are neither mapped nor pending, and every original comment and declared test method has an explicit disposition.

Reviewed all eighteen SingleThreadEventLoop declarations (seventeen native mappings plus one caller-promise/listener decision) and all three AbstractEventLoop declarations with real re-registration, default/assigned executor identity and 600 ms zero-quiet termination. Corrected polymorphic ordinary/tail queue accounting. Added native registration counts/snapshots and suspension admission with lifetime/migration/failure tests; reviewed all seven NioEventLoop own declarations with explicit backend decisions. Ported both MultiThreadIoEventLoopGroup tests and connected the auto-scaling chooser to native registered channels, utilization, suspended-worker admission and shutdown. Ported the caller-owned manual pump and eleven portable source methods, with real TCP and channel-migration contracts. Separated manual inbound I/O and task phases and ported four original I/O-handler count and manual-listener methods. Ported pending connect and write completion dispatch with the six outbound source declarations and eight native contract cases. Threaded socket completion phases and the source task-processing I/O ratio are implemented. Added direct completion registration, backend compatibility and chooser-preserving queries. UDP preparation and delivery share one completion callback. Ported all portable AbstractChannelTest declarations, preserving initial write-failure causes, close-before-release ownership and inactive-flush reentrancy. Added Task-native channel-correlated group failures and fixed duplicate-member stayClosed admission. Shared output-shutdown policy now handles generic channels and TCP consistently, with admission closed before native shutdown, scoped producer ownership and the full-close default. Channel groups expose immutable per-channel native Task snapshots with live completion and typed id removal. Connected channel/native-Task transfer progress to IProgress with original totals, owner emission, observer isolation and the Common executor observation bridge. Added the original deregistration/read-clear regression.

stages.name: Bootstrap, Resolver integration and TCP
stages.completedUnit: Native Bootstrap/ServerBootstrap, real TCP connect/accept/read/write and all five NioSocketChannel originals; all six ServerBootstrap declarations and all nineteen Bootstrap declarations reviewed (eighteen original mappings plus one explicit JVM-only failure-promise representation decision). Live client/parent/child configuration views, immutable ordered snapshots, source volatile visibility, resolver default/disable/reset/clone state, late-registration bind/connect and asynchronous resolution are covered alongside scoped initializer extensions and cancellation independent of a pending resolver producer. Added six original self/peer shutdown declarations and three selected SocketHalfClosed declarations with 28 explicit allocator/role/read variants; manual batching, final input-read notification, output-first shutdown and queued-write ownership are implemented. Completed review of all eight SocketHalfClosed declarations: seven mappings (one conditional Unix-only reset fixture) and one original backend-capability exclusion. TCP error policy, queued cause/ownership and abortive zero-linger close are ported; all original fixture comments are preserved. Added BCL socket ownership constructors, server message allocator selection, actual bounded accept batches, partial delivery/error ordering and recoverable/fatal accept handling; original server and inherited option fixtures are reviewed. Added AF_UNIX stream/listener implementations and original domain fixtures, plus the portable TCP echo methods and supplemental domain half-close, cleanup and echo tests. Ported real TCP and AF_UNIX gathering writes, partial vector accounting, flush boundaries and all six gathering-write source declarations. Ported Linux TCP peer authentication and deferred source-port allocation with the original MD5 fixture. Ported the complete SocketConnectTest fixture and the native Linux client Fast Open path. Ported the five socket read-state/EOF fixtures (seven source declarations and sixteen allocator/route cases), retaining original quiet windows, receive budgets, integer decode and the paused 32 MiB EOF digest. Pre-activation manual reads are preserved. Ported all eleven declarations in SocketFileRegion, SocketBufRelease, SocketExceptionHandling, SocketCloseForcibly and SocketConditionalWritability fixtures. Fixed logical FileRegion completion/resume, owner progress and nonblocking Stream transfer with real backpressure/close lifetime coverage. Added native default-file handle/range sends with original file identity/cursor/progress/lifetime, safe portable fallback, and all seven inherited domain file-region scenarios (fourteen allocator rows). Added the shared IDuplexChannel/IsShutdown API, original TCP/domain address scenarios, inherited domain initial-read and peer-shutdown fixtures, the complete 100-connection descriptor-reuse body and registration-before-write original. Restored real-network connection-attempt originals and implemented the measured Windows AF_UNIX EOF workaround. Channel groups expose native ISet bulk operations and ordinal-name/identity ordering while preserving Id admission, automatic removal, stayClosed and server-first snapshots. Corrected separate TCP stream/listener option admission, platform backlog defaults/visibility, JDK positive buffer sizes and linger clamp, one-time best-effort NoDelay defaults and Linux IPv6 traffic-class configuration. Repeated the original native/domain config tests without changing their mappings. Scalar ByteBuf sends now share the original per-pass writeSpinCount with vectors, including zero-cost empty buffers, partial progress and native borrow lifetime. Source write-method names and reviewed TCP test identifiers are aligned. Eligible file-region writes now share the original per-attempt spin quantum, including zero-progress retry, physical/logical completion separation, native partial errors and close-owned borrows. The protected DoWriteFileRegion producer retains source identifiers and original comments.
stages.next: Continue remaining portable socket and selector/backend contracts against their original fixtures and runtime comments.

stages.name: UDP and remaining portable transport contracts
stages.completedUnit: Native UDP datagram send/receive/truncation and original 100-channel bind; all ten DatagramUnicast methods, port-only Inet binding and IPv4 multicast with 46 explicit family/allocator executions. Family-backed multicast options, ASM membership, IPv4 source membership/blocking, registered-only sends/reconnect and recoverable/fatal read-error contracts are covered. Pending-write/coalescing and original channel-pool fixtures remain recorded in their own entries. Added native UDP receive batches and the complete IPv4-mapped unicast fixture with 22 original allocator cases. Added IPv6 source multicast operations and two original Unix ICMP fixtures. The inherited IPv6 multicast fixture and the Linux IPv6 traffic class mapping are verified. Linux UDP disconnect preserves its socket and local binding across reconnect. Linux validates all eight Unix TCP reset cases. Linux dual-mode IPv4 multicast membership and per-socket multicast delivery are verified with shared-port packet tests. Mapped six original epoll datagram scenarios to the portable CLR receive path. Ported segmented sends, Linux UDP GRO, and native receive batching with five original tests. Mapped original destination metadata, IP_FREEBIND, and the mixed-family multicast source scenario with its Linux route limitation. Linux UDP and TCP listeners now expose kernel port sharing. TCP listener and stream native configuration fixtures are mapped. Connected MAX_MESSAGES_PER_WRITE to native UDP write passes, including recoverable failures, cancellation, config snapshots and readied I/O/task phases; fixed empty/cancelled-buffer native sends and private-config registration assumptions. Repeated both original unicast fixtures and their allocator variants on Windows/Linux.

review.scope: channel(Class<? extends C> channelClass) maps to Channel(Type channelClass) with its original comment and checkNotNull(channelClass, "channelClass"), creating a ReflectiveChannelFactory; the generic Channel<T>() uses the same path, so constructor failures become ChannelException as in the source. The native error-policy fixture verifies both flushed tasks retain original exception identity, unflushed close retains its cause, and all owned buffers release after an in-flight failure. Reviewed adaptive gathering limits against pinned NioSocketChannel and ChannelOutboundBuffer: scalar accepted-byte results now adjust the next window; vector maxBytes remains a whole-message hint and includes the first message without slicing segments. SO_SNDBUF updates recalculate the native-derived limit. Java signed-int shift boundaries are preserved in checked C# builds. A stale asynchronous completion cannot replace newer explicit configuration. Seventeen supplemental cases are separate from existing original mappings. Source-named gathering/configuration methods and NioBuffers/NioBufferCount/NioBufferSize retain CLR memory types; six existing original buffer-view tests retain source variable names and assertions. Writability uses the source methods: incrementPendingOutboundBytes(size)/decrementPendingOutboundBytes(size) notify later, the buffer entry paths pass invokeLater=false, setUserDefinedWritability/clearUserDefinedWritability always notify later, writabilityMask throws ArgumentException with the source message. CLR: the single-argument methods stay public; a closed buffer suppresses later notifications as the source null buffer reference does. 2026-11-17 structure port: ChannelOutboundBuffer follows the pinned Java class member by member: the flushedEntry/unflushedEntry/tailEntry singly linked Entry list with its flushed count; addMessage/addFlush/current/currentProgress/progress/remove()/remove(Throwable)/remove0/removeEntry/removeBytes; Entry instances recycled through the Common Recycler (newInstance, cancel(), unguardedRecycle, unguardedRecycleAndGetNext, pendingSize = size + CHANNEL_OUTBOUND_BUFFER_ENTRY_OVERHEAD, the count/buf/bufs caches); nioBuffers()/nioBuffers(int, long) over the thread-local NIO_BUFFERS array (FastThreadLocal) with expandNioBufferArray and the per-entry single segment or segment array; clearNioBuffers as in the source (nioBufferSize is not reset); writability through totalPendingSize and unwritable (Interlocked for the field updaters) and the cached fireChannelWritabilityChangedTask; failFlushed, close(Throwable, boolean) with its two precondition checks and the inFail deferral to the event loop, close(ClosedChannelException); safeSuccess/safeFail with the PromiseNotificationUtil log messages; the deprecated no-op recycle(); bytesBeforeUnwritable/bytesBeforeWritable; forEachFlushedMessage with the IMessageProcessor interface. CLR adaptations: the queued write's Task is the promise (WritePromise, a TaskCompletionSource): the caller's CancellationToken cancels it until addFlush() calls setUncancellable(), and a token cancelled before the write is queued fails it at once and releases the message; the IProgress<ChannelWriteProgress> observer captured with the write stands for ChannelProgressivePromise with the tryProgress(progress, total) checks; ByteBuffer views are borrowed ReadOnlyMemory<byte> segments of ByteBuf.AsReadOnlySequence(...) (nioBufferCount() is the segment count, one for a contiguous buffer), and as ReadOnlyMemory has no position a cached view is advanced by the bytes removeBytes(...) consumed; IllegalStateException is InvalidOperationException; removeBytes(...) throws for written bytes beyond the flushed buffers (the source asserts) unless a handler closed the buffer; the channel keeps this object after close, so a closed flag stands for the source's null outboundBuffer and close(...) drops its references to recycled entries. AbstractChannel's close, closeForcibly, registration-failure and shutdownOutput paths call failFlushed(cause, false) and then close(...) as AbstractUnsafe does (closeOutboundBufferForShutdown uses close(cause, true)). All 98 original comments are at their C# counterparts. The supplemental ChannelOutboundBufferContractTest covers partial-write segment caching, the per-thread NIO_BUFFERS array, the close preconditions, close(...) deferred from failFlushed(...) and forEachFlushedMessage; ChannelWriteProgressContractTest closes the buffer from a progress observer with failFlushed(cause, false) and close(cause, true).

review.scope: Reviewed original read budgets/coalescing/manual-read wakeups plus connect/close ownership and write ordering against all 32 LocalChannelTest declarations. Native cancellation closes a pending client without touching the server-owned queued peer. Explicit local addresses are honored even after an earlier bind. A synchronous local bind failure or refused connect closes the channel and releases the registered address. Closed connect and peer-closed writes fail with ClosedChannelException as in close and doWrite, replacing the earlier IOException("Channel is closed."/"Peer is closed."). 2026-11-17 structure port: LocalChannel follows the pinned Java class: the State machine (OPEN/BOUND/CONNECTED/CLOSED, null until bound or connected) updated with Interlocked as STATE_UPDATER does; readTask and finishReadTask; inboundBuffer; doBind, doDisconnect and doClose with closedFrom, the peer hand-off through peer.eventLoop().execute(tryClose(peerIsActive)) and its rejection fallback; tryClose; readInbound with buffer coalescing; doBeginRead with readInProgress and the MAX_READER_STACK_DEPTH bound kept in InternalThreadLocalMap; doWrite(ChannelOutboundBuffer) with writeInProgress (AbstractChannel flush0() now calls it for this transport); finishPeerRead, runFinishTask0, runFinishPeerReadTask and finishPeerRead0 with finishReadFuture; releaseInboundBuffers; LocalUnsafe registered(), unregistered(), closeNow() and connect(...). CLR adaptations: reference State constants keep the enum's null initial state; AbstractChannel's active flag follows the CONNECTED state (isOpen()/isActive() combine both); LocalUnsafe.connect(...) overrides the folded AbstractUnsafe.connect(...) and its Task is connectPromise; AlreadyConnectedException, ConnectionPendingException, NotYetConnectedException and ConnectException are SocketException with SocketError.IsConnected, AlreadyInProgress, NotConnected and ConnectionRefused (with the source messages); ConcurrentQueue replaces the SPSC queue; submit(...) is SubmitAsync, whose rejected Task is rethrown as submit(...) throws; a CancellationToken still aborts a pending connect by closing the channel; a gate orders a writer's inboundBuffer add with this channel's state change in doClose(), so a retained message is never published into an already drained queue. All 64 original comments are at their C# counterparts. Tests: testConnectedAlready asserts SocketError.IsConnected; the supplemental LocalChannelOwnershipContractTest adds connection-pending, refused-message and reader-stack-depth cases, and its reentrant write case and LocalCoalescingContractTest hook the message release in in.remove() instead of the removed per-message write-completion hook.

review.scope: Process queued UDP packets in a bounded receive cycle using the allocator message budget. Membership identity uses the address bytes and interface, matching Java IPv6 address equality. Linux ICMP receive and write behavior is verified by the original allocator rows. On Linux UDP disconnect detaches the peer from the same socket and restores the original ephemeral port when necessary. Linux dual-mode sockets use IPv4 multicast membership operations for IPv4 groups and mirror relevant socket configuration across both IP levels. A native connect error closes the datagram channel, preserving the original socket failure. Preparation, allocator accounting and delivery of ready UDP packets now share one I/O callback. A follow-up receive that is still pending starts the next batch; the loop rechecks read admission before delivery. Linux optional recvmsg and recvmmsg use the same owner delivery phase and retain exact UDP segment slices. Linux UDP uses per-packet original destination metadata when enabled, falling back to the bound address when absent. Implemented the original message-channel MAX_MESSAGES_PER_WRITE quantum with a per-pass snapshot and per-entry accounting, including continued write failures and cancelled empty placeholders. UDP re-arms the next native I/O phase, allowing ordinary work without admitting unflushed writes. Byte-stream, local and embedded policies are unchanged. Native writer/borrow ownership remains exclusive through asynchronous resumption. Datagram zero-length buffers complete without a send, matching NioDatagramChannel.doWriteMessage; receiving externally sent empty datagrams is unchanged. Custom configs use the public budget option or the original unlimited fallback and optional active-on-registration lookup, without a private-config registration cast. Family constructors NioDatagramChannel(SocketProtocolFamily) and the deprecated InternetProtocolFamily overload keep the original parameter names. Checked arithmetic retains Java long-counter wraparound and invalid reports are suppressed. No final progress is invented for transports that do not call Progress. Built-in optimized writes and explicit native-capability probes opt in; existing custom whole-message overrides remain honored. The eligible built-in/native-capability file path now uses source-named DoWriteFileRegion(region), preserving position and localFlushedAmount. DoWriteInternal shares its snapshotted writeSpinCount across ByteBuf and file producer attempts: already-complete regions cost zero, accepted positive transfers cost one, and zero transfer returns WRITE_STATUS_SNDBUF_FULL for a later turn. Logical transferred() controls completion independently of physical accepted bytes. The native producer submits at most one bounded file-handle range; the Stream fallback invokes TransferTo once on a worker. Partial native errors still record accepted bytes/progress before failure; unsupported zero-byte capability rejection resumes safely through TransferTo. Worker borrows survive close/stop until the producer returns. Native output closure is checked before new work. notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: AbstractChannelHandlerContext.isNotValidPromise rejects promise.channel()!=channel()
notApplicableMethods.reason: CLR outbound methods accept EndPoint/message/CancellationToken and return consumer Tasks. Callers cannot submit a mutable producer belonging to another channel; that invalid input is absent from the public API.

notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: isNotValidPromise rejects VoidChannelPromise for close
notApplicableMethods.reason: The CLR API has no VoidChannelPromise argument or void producer object. CloseAsync always returns a normal observable Task; manufacturing this input would add the JVM facade the port deliberately avoids.

notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: isNotValidPromise rejects AbstractChannel.CloseFuture supplied as an operation promise
notApplicableMethods.reason: CloseCompletion is a consumer-only Task with no public setter, and CloseAsync has no completion-producer parameter. A close-notification Task cannot be supplied as a mutable close-operation producer.

notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: validateWrite releases referenceCounted when a wrong-channel promise argument is rejected before transport ownership
notApplicableMethods.reason: The sole rejection trigger in this original helper is channel2.newPromise() supplied to channel1.write. No such parameter exists in CLR WriteAsync. Its exact validation/reference-release scenario is inapplicable, not replaced by an unrelated handler-throw test. Existing native cancellation and rejected-dispatch tests separately cover supported input ownership.

notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: validateWrite releases referenceCounted when wrong-channel promise is supplied to writeAndFlush
notApplicableMethods.reason: WriteAndFlushAsync likewise accepts no completion producer, so a foreign-channel promise cannot enter validation. Do not pretend a generic write failure is the original scenario; supported cancellation/rejection ownership remains separately tested.

notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: ensurePromiseUseCorrectExecutor cascades a context-owned DefaultChannelPromise into a caller-supplied foreign-executor promise; six attached listeners observe context ownership
notApplicableMethods.reason: Native Tasks expose no executor-bearing mutable promise input and do not automatically schedule callbacks on a channel. This exact cascade is absent. A separately counted native test completes all six operations from a foreign producer and explicitly regains the handler owner before observing state; it is a CLR alternative, not the original assertion ported unchanged.

notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: VoidChannelPromise.tryFailure routes a write failure to ExceptionCaught without a returned completion future
notApplicableMethods.reason: Every CLR write returns an observable Task, so there is no explicit VoidChannelPromise failure-notification mode. The native alternative awaits that Task and preserves the original exception identity; it does not manually fire ExceptionCaught to simulate the absent API.

notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: Registration listener initializes OioSocketChannel on a dedicated OioEventLoopGroup
notApplicableMethods.reason: CLR Transport has one asynchronous System.Net.Sockets NioSocketChannel, not a separate obsolete JVM blocking OIO channel/event-loop family. The mapped NIO registration test executes the same portable listener contract on the actual CLR TCP implementation. Running that identical CLR case twice would not port an OIO backend.

notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: Register a caller-supplied channel-associated Java ChannelPromise after loop shutdown. Its monitor/future completes with RejectedExecutionException and its channel closes, but assertFalse(latch.await(1 second)) requires that the already-attached listener never runs because dispatch through the stopped channel executor is rejected. The source comment says notified while the assertion explicitly requires non-notification.
notApplicableMethods.reason: Native RegisterAsync returns a Task and has no mutable caller-supplied Java promise input. Task consumers can observe a fault through the CLR scheduler even after the event loop stops. Faking a promise/listener executor or silently changing the one-second non-notification assertion would change the source contract. Review the whole original method separately without a mapped count or xUnit skip; the positive native consumer/closure counterpart is supplementary. Java executes the unchanged original, including its one-second negative listener observation.

review.scope: All eighteen declarations reviewed: seventeen mapped executions plus one Java caller-producer/listener non-notification contract.
